subject: MSA addendum: private hosting attestation & evidence handoff pathway
messages:
From: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@acmehealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: 2025-09-04T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private hosting requirements & addendum question

Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement and legal teams have started pulling together requirements for a private hosting engagement (VPC deployment with isolated control plane). Two quick asks from legal before we escalate to commercial:

1) Confirmation of license scope for private hosting: we need language that explicitly states production runtime access for Acme employees only, and that Redwood will not claim derivative rights to customer data or embeddings.
2) Evidence / attestation options: our security team prefers a deterministic path for audit evidence. Can Redwood provide either (A) a witnessed snapshot + custody attestation, or (B) a time-limited remote inspection window with notarized access logs?
3) If you have a short MSA addendum draft that covers these options, please attach — it will save cycles.

I've attached our high-level hosting requirements (Acme_Hosting_Requirements.pdf).

Would appreciate a short note on the preferred operational pattern and an ETA on redlines.

Thanks,
Taylor Reed
Director, Cloud Security
Acme Health

Attachments: Acme_Hosting_Requirements.pdf

From: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
To: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@acmehealth.com>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: 2025-09-04T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Private hosting requirements & addendum question

Taylor —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front:

- License scope: Redwood's standard private-deploy addendum supports customer-exclusive production access and we do not take ownership of customer data or derived embeddings — we can insert explicit language.
- Evidence options: both patterns you listed are supported operationally. We typically offer a "witnessed snapshot + attest" flow for on-prem or air-gapped, and a "time-limited console inspection" for VPC deployments. Each has trade-offs on operator involvement and transfer of cryptographic material (KMS).

I've attached a first-pass addendum that frames both options and highlights where KMS custody/lifecycle language would live: Redwood_Private_Addendum_draft.docx.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll loop in Legal (marissa_cole) for redlines;
- Can you confirm whether Acme prefers an actual snapshot transfer vs. remote inspection? Either is fine but procurement/legal often have a clear preference.
- If acceptable, we can schedule a 30-min triage call with security + legal next week to align on the chosen path.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Redwood_Private_Addendum_draft.docx

From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
To: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@acmehealth.com>, david_kim@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2025-09-05T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Private hosting requirements & addendum question — internal redlines

Jonas — looping in with internal redlines and suggested carve-outs. Posting highlights here so we can keep the external thread tidy. Full redline attached (Redlines_20250904.docx).

Key points / proposed language snippets:
1) License scope: Add: "Customer retains all right, title, and interest in Customer Data and Model Outputs; Redwood grants Customer a non-exclusive, perpetual license to use any Redwood-delivered operational artifacts solely for Customer's internal production operations." (This avoids transfer of derivative ownership.)
2) Operator access: For VPC deployments, prefer: "Operator access for troubleshooting is by exception and requires (i) Customer-initiated temporary access token; (ii) two-person Redwood approval; and (iii) detailed access logs provided to Customer within 48 hours."
3) Audit / evidence: Define two mutually exclusive exhibits: Exhibit A — Witnessed Snapshot & Sealed Transfer; Exhibit B — Time-Limited Remote Inspection. Each exhibit will enumerate artifacts to be produced, the notarization/attestation language, and retention periods.
4) KMS custody: Offer either (i) customer-managed KMS with HSM, or (ii) split-key escrow for the narrow purpose of emergency rollback with on-demand auditing — redlines include strict use limitations and destruction timelines.
5) Indemnity/liability: tighten language around data exposure during witness events; require Redwood to carry additional cyber liability for events during the window.

Action items for external thread: please ask Acme to pick Exhibit A or B and confirm if they require a sealed-transfer notarization. If they prefer Exhibit A we will propose a short security validation runbook (to be attached).

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Redlines_20250904.docx

From: legal@acmehealth.com
To: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com; jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2025-09-07T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Private hosting requirements & addendum question

Marissa / Jonas —

Thanks for the fast turn. Acme Legal has discussed internally and our preferred path is Exhibit B (Time-Limited Remote Inspection) for the initial deployment. A few points and a counter-proposal attached: Acme_counter_redlines.pdf.

Counterpoints:
- Console access: require that the temporary credentials be scoped to read-only, time-limited (max 4 hours), and logged to an append-only audit sink under Customer control.
- Notarization: we are not asking for notarized sealed-transfers at this stage due to procurement timelines, but we do require a cryptographic notarization of logs (SHA256 + timestamped signature) for each inspection window.
- KMS: we prefer customer-managed KMS for production keys; however, for ephemeral rollback proofs we can accept an escrow arrangement if the escrow uses a neutral third-party custodian and is subject to strict access controls.

We attached detailed redlines to the addendum and a proposed inspection runbook for the remote window. Please confirm Redwood's acceptance (or comments).

Best,
Lydia Gómez
Sr. Counsel, Acme Health
legal@acmehealth.com

Attachments: Acme_counter_redlines.pdf

From: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
To: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@acmehealth.com>, legal@acmehealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, david_kim@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2025-09-08T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Private hosting requirements & addendum question — next steps

Thanks, Lydia & Taylor —

Good alignment. Summary and proposed next steps:

1) Acme selects Exhibit B (Time-Limited Remote Inspection) — Redwood accepts the scope in principle.
2) We will update the addendum to: (a) specify read-only, time-limited token pattern (4-hour max), (b) require append-only audit sink under Customer control, and (c) include cryptographic notarization clause (SHA256 + signed timestamp) for each inspection.
3) KMS: we will offer customer-managed KMS for production; for escrowed ephemeral rollback keys we'll propose a neutral custodian (we use [independent custodian] as an option) and add strict access audit language.
4) Timeline & call: propose 30-min legal + security sync on 2025-09-11 at 10:00 AM PT to finalize updated addendum and runbook. Please confirm availability.

I'll attach the updated addendum and a short inspection-runbook for the call by end of day Monday. Once legal is aligned we can move to an expedited order form and signature (DocuSign).

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: (will follow)
